newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH SHARES EXTEND GAINS, SEEN DOWN ON THURSDAY.
newsitem.headline: POLISH SHARES EXTEND GAINS, SEEN DOWN ON THURSDAY.

text.p: Polish shares extended Tuesday's gains but analysts said the stronger selling after price-fixing and falls in continuous trade signalled the market was not yet ready to break out of its current stabilisation.
Analysts expected a fall on Thursday and said prices were apparently still too high after the bourse's growth by more than 25 percent this year.
"The market is pretty expensive and there's not a big group of investors who would want to enter at current prices for the long term," said Roman Sosnowski, an analyst at Bank Staropolski brokerage.
The main market's all-share WIG index rose 0.6 percent to 17,830.2 points and turnover rose 23 percent to 241.2 million zlotys on both markets.

Ryszard Wojnowski, an analyst at Polish Investment Bank (PBI) brokerage, said recent gains by small-cap firms would likely continue, with those firms enjoying a prospective 1997 p/e ratio of around eight versus 14 for blue chips.
Analysts said 17,000 points provided support though Staropolski's Sosnowski said a fall toward 16,000 was possible.

Analysts said Espebepe fell 10 percent after a newspaper article on Wednesday said one of the firm's creditors would seek the firm's bankruptcy in court. The bourse said Espebepe will not trade on Friday, when its creditors meet.

They said top gainer Indykpol's low liquidity led to an exaggerated 10 percent surge while 9.8-percent gainer Kable was likely helped by Tuesday's news it expected to lift net profit in 1997 about four times from 1996.
NFI units fell 2.4 percent at the regular session and fell 0.6 percent in live trade, where the WIG 20 index fell 1.7 percent. -- Steven Silber +48 22 653 9700
